dedupe_keys.name: national rail data feeds darwin real time train running knowledgebase historic service performance great britain

description: National Rail offers application programming interfaces and XML feeds for third-party developers, derived from three engines. Darwin is the Great Britain rail industry's official train running information engine, providing real-time arrival and departure predictions, platform numbers, delay estimates, schedule changes and cancellations, and it drives the Historic Service Performance web service with what happened to services up to one year ago. Knowledgebase holds static and real-time information such as station facilities, service disruption and engineering work, and the Online Journey Planner computes routes, fares and ticket availability. Coverage is national for the GB passenger rail network. Knowledgebase is available as XML through self sign-up and a REST API, the journey planner feeds are SOAP APIs under formal licence, and other feeds are requested through a data feed request form or the Rail Data Marketplace, which mixes open-by-default and commercial data products. Caveats: no single open licence is stated, access needs registration, and attribution must follow National Rail brand guidelines. The feeds support delay propagation and resilience analysis of rail disruption, timetable-based network models and passenger information in digital twins. They complement the Network Rail open data feeds catalogued here.
